title: vendor-unification-sprint-planning-to-redwood-api
next_steps: Redwood to send POC runbook and pricing sheet by 2025-05-13
HorizonMetrics to provide 3 representative endpoints and sample traffic profile by 2025-05-16
Schedule 1-hour benchmark kickoff with infra + SEs week of 2025-05-19
action_items: Lena Park: send security docs (SOC2 summary, encryption & KMS notes) - due 2025-05-13
Marco Diaz: prepare sample benchmark script that mirrors HorizonMetrics streaming + long context - due 2025-05-15
Tom Li: share endpoint list and tokenization details - due 2025-05-16
summary: Discovery + migration-demo focused on unifying multiple vendor endpoints (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together) to Redwood API. Covered parity mapping, streaming/func-call equivalence, latency/cost tradeoffs, and POC plan. Customer requested security artifacts and a benchmark sprint. Agreed next steps and owners.
topics: parity mapping: model and API surface
dedicated vs hosted and VPC considerations
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for hopping on, i think yall have the agenda i sent? um quick intros then we'll walk through a parity map and a proposed sprint plan
[00:12] Priya Singh (HorizonMetrics - CTO): yep thanks lena. i'm priya, with tom and amir. main thing for us is consolidate runtime providers, lower stack complexity and predictable cost. timeline is tight, Q3 pilot ideally.
[00:26] Marco Diaz (Redwood SE): great. quick note, i'll demo how we map openai-style calls and also how together/anthropic differences look in practice. i know some names get munged in transcripts so bear with me.
[00:40] Tom Li (HorizonMetrics - ML Eng): quick context: most endpoints are gpt-4 style chat + some embedding endpoints. we also have a few long-document streaming endpoints (20k tokens), and some function-call hooks. current traffic pattern: spiky with long tails.
[00:56] Amir Rahman (Platform): plus data residency, we need logs to stay in our EU account; and audit retention is 2 years.
[01:06] Lena Park: perfect. so first slide — parity map. (brief sigh) so redwood exposes a single API that handles text-gen, chat, embeddings, rerank. for openai chat -> we map messages->messages, content->content, function-calls are supported via our tool-calling shim, slight naming diffs.
[01:28] Marco Diaz: also with streaming, our chunked event stream is similar to openai's chunking but we include token-level latencies headers for tracing. for together/anthropic where the prompt model style differs, we translate context to prompt templates and preserve system instruction semantics.
[01:46] Priya: okay how often do we see hallucination differences when swapping models? any regressions in behavior when we reduce quantization to save cost?
[02:00] Marco: good question. quantization can introduce slight score/response variability; we recommend a gold set of prompts and run A/B on quality. optimize (the console) has eval hooks to make that automated.
[02:15] Priya: can you show the console bit? we want to see how we'd detect regressions.
[02:20] Marco: sure, i'll share my screen. (pause, 10s) all right, console -> optimize -> evals. here you upload prompt set, baseline is your current provider, we run comparisons and give delta metrics (token-level latency, top-1 exact match, embedding cosine drift). note this is integrated with alerts so you can fail a rollout if quality drops.
[02:47] Tom: does it hook into our CI? we have a pipeline that triggers tests on model changes.
[02:52] Marco: yes, there's an API and webhooks. you can gate deploys. we'll provide a sample github action in the poc runbook.
[02:58] Priya: talk about cost — we pay per token with openai now, shifting to Redwood what's the typical delta?
[03:06] Lena: depends on model family and quantization. in many cases teams see 20-60% lower per-token cost using our recommended quantized variants and batching. but for strict tail-latency needs possibly dedicated pools which are commit-based.
[03:22] Amir: we need predictable p95 under 150ms for mimic endpoints, currently on openai we see 120ms p95 but at off hours it's inconsistent. how would you guarantee that?
[03:33] Marco: two levers: dedicated capacity with reserved GPU pools and routing policies, or hosted with autoscaling + higher tier SLA. you can pin a model variant and set canary fallbacks so if a pool degrades we route to a cheaper variant but keep latency SLO via autoscaling.
[03:49] Lena: note that canary fallback works across regions too so if eu pool is saturated you can fall back to eu+1 or dedicated for critical traffic.
[03:58] Tom: on the function calls — our code uses openai function_call semantics heavily. what's the migration path?
[04:05] Marco: we have a function-call shim: names map 1:1, and you can detect calls with the same trigger. some edge cases with nested objects need small adaptor code (we'll include a snippet). streaming function-calls behave like streaming completions — we stream partial JSON and then a final call result.
[04:26] Priya: the big ask: data never leaves our VPC logs plain-text. can you operate in a private deployment?
[04:33] Lena: yes — Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packaging. control plane can be customer-managed; logs can be pushed to your S3 or KMS-wrapped buckets. we'll note SOC2 and integration points in the security pack.
[04:46] Amir: encryption at rest with our KMS is required. any HSM options?
[04:49] Marco: yes we support KMS integrations and HSM via our private offering. we'll share the HSM notes.
[04:55] Priya: ok demo time — can you show a live parity call from an openai-style request to redwood?
[05:01] Marco: sure. (types) making a chat request mapped from openai payload. sending... (short pause) response comes back streaming. see the event with metadata header and token deltas.
[05:16] Tom: looks similar. i hear you emit trace-id per token?
[05:20] Marco: per-chunk timestamps, yes. helps root-cause slow token generation.
[05:25] Priya: what about embeddings differences — our semantic-search relies on cosine thresholds we tuned on openai ada embeddings. do you repro those embeddings?
[05:33] Marco: embeddings vary across models; we provide embedding compatibility mapping and we'll run an embedding drift check as part of the benchmark. sometimes you need a small re-threshold or a lightweight reindex with drift-aware mapping.
[05:45] Lena: for the POC we propose: 1) Redwood runs a 3-day benchmark on your 3 top endpoints, mirroring your traffic (we'll need endpoint list and sample payloads), 2) we run cost + latency + quality comparisons and produce a parity report, 3) recommend quantization and routing plan.
[06:05] Priya: timeline?
[06:07] Lena: kickoff next week, benchmark week of 5/19, report by 5/26.
[06:12] Amir: who owns infra changes? we have a central infra team (me) that will need runbooks and terraform modules.
[06:18] Lena: we can supply terraform modules for private/dedicated and a sample helm chart for on-prem. Marco will prepare the infra runbook.
[06:26] Marco: noted — i'll include sample terraform + eks helm values.
[06:29] Tom: can you also run a long-context streaming test? that's our biggest pain point.
[06:33] Marco: yes, include that in the benchmark script. we'll mimic your 20k token sessions with prefix caching enabled. highlight: Redwood's KV cache lets you avoid re-encoding large context for repeated prefixes which saves cost.
[06:48] Priya: how does prefix caching interact with privacy/regulatory needs?
[06:52] Marco: prefix cache is configurable; for sensitive content you can disable caching or use ephemeral session caches that never persist to disk. in private deployments you can enforce enclave-only caches.
[07:05] Lena: quick question from me — do you have any internal quotas or rate limiting we should know about?
[07:08] Amir: we throttle at 600 RPS at peak but we burst up to 1200 occasionally. most calls are small but some long-session calls occupy capacity for longer.
[07:19] Marco: that helps sizing. for dedicated pools we'll run capacity planning to estimate the GPU count and batch sizes to hit your p95 target.
[07:29] Priya: any concerns about simultaneous function-calls and streaming? we sometimes call functions that then spin off more model calls.
[07:36] Marco: orchestration is tricky; we recommend a local async queue that batches outbound model calls and we have guidance on concurrency limits in the runbook. can include sample code.
[07:45] Priya: ok show me the console again — routing rules and fallbacks.
[07:48] Marco: (screen) here: routing -> policies. you can build a rule: if model p95 > 200ms and region eu saturated -> fallback to dedicated eu-fallback. you can also set cost caps to move less-critical traffic to quantized variants.
[08:07] Tom: is there a way to simulate the cost tradeoff per million tokens in the console?
[08:11] Marco: cost calculator — yes you can plug in throughput, sequence length distribution and it returns a per-million token estimate across variants. we'll share a pre-filled sheet for your workloads.
[08:22] Priya: what's the failure mode for rollouts? do you support automatic rollback?
[08:26] Marco: yes — rollout policies can be configured to auto-rollback if quality metrics fall beyond a threshold. you can also do canary percentages and progressive ramp.
[08:36] Amir: regarding logs — we need audit logs for 2 years on access and SSE events. is that straightforward?
[08:41] Lena: yes, audit logs are available; for private deployments we integrate with your SIEM. for hosted we can stream logs to your secure bucket.
[08:51] Priya: security pack?
[08:53] Lena: i'll attach SOC2 summary, encryption notes, KMS/HSM integration guide, and data residency checklist.
[08:58] Tom: ok i want to call out one risk — embeddings drift on replacement might force us to reindex a lot of data. can the benchmark tell us reindex effort?
[09:07] Marco: we'll include delta histograms and a recommended reindex strategy (partial reindex, rethresholding, or hybrid embeddings).
[09:16] Priya: great. let's talk POC acceptance criteria.
[09:18] Lena: propose: parity on 3 endpoints where top-1 accuracy difference < 2% and p95 latency within 20% of baseline and cost <= baseline or with acceptable savings per your SRE team. if not met, we iterate with quantization knobs or different model variants.
[09:36] Amir: that seems reasonable. one more item — SSO and RBAC integration. we use SAML and Okta.
[09:44] Marco: supported. we'll provide SAML SSO guide and role-based access config.
[09:50] Priya: any legal hoops — data processors, subprocessors?
[09:53] Lena: we'll provide DPA and subprocessors list in the legal packet. for private deployments subprocessors are limited since control plane can be customer-managed.
[10:03] Tom: loop in our procurement — they'll need pricing bands for hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[10:09] Lena: noted. i'll include tiered pricing in the follow-up.
[10:13] Marco: small demo note — function-call mappings require one small client adapter for nested JSONs; i'll paste snippet in the runbook.
[10:21] Priya: ok final ask: can you run a worst-case tail test where we spike with 1000 concurrent long sessions?
[10:28] Marco: yes, we'll fiber that into load test plan and show degradation curves.
[10:34] Lena: recap of next steps: we send POC runbook + pricing + security pack by Tue 5/13, Horizon sends endpoints + sample payloads by 5/16, kickoff benchmark week of 5/19.
[10:46] Priya: thanks all. appreciate the pragmatic plan.
[10:50] Amir: thanks, look forward to the runbook.
[10:52] Lena: great, we'll follow up. thanks everyone.
[10:56] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript has intermittent speaker attribution issues (some filler labeled as Marco when earlier speaker may have spoken). Shared artifacts: "POC runbook (shared link)"; "security-pack.pdf (shared link)"; "benchmark-template.xlsx (shared link)".
